newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end higher across the board.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures extended early gains to end higher across the board on Friday, as buying gathered force reflecting the yen's weakness against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 15 yen to 21 yen per gram higher, with benchmark June ending up 19 at 1,162 yen.

"Private investors hunted for bargains. Trade houses sold gold futures which were relatively higher than dollar-based gold, and bought spot gold in arbitrage deals," one trader said. Spot gold was quoted at $320.65/321.15 per ounce at 0714 GMT, against $319.60/320.10 in New York on Thursday.
"Spot gold which looked oversold, firmed during Asian hours. If support at $320 per ounce proves strong, further short-covering may emerge," the trader said.
However, the long-term outlook for gold remains bearish amid concern over more central bank gold sales, traders said.

Platinum group metals (PGMs) climbed further in the afternoon session on animated short-covering. In palladium, the December, February and April contracts surged by their 22 yen per gram daily limit by the close, they said.
"The palladium futures market is still heavily short. Volatile trade may continue," one trader said.
Short positions in TOCOM palladium totalled around 61 tonnes as of Thursday, which is equivalent of about 30 percent of the world's palladium supply in 1996.

Russia has resumed its PGMs exports this year but persistant concerns over the stability of Russian supplies next year are seen as a bullish factor for the market. Palladium futures ranged from 12 to 22 yen per gram up with benchmark June palladium was 19 higher at 524 yen. Platinum was 12 to 26 yen higher. Benchmark June platinum was up 12 yen at 1,305 yen.
Benchmark June silver was up 3.0 yen per 10 grams at 162.2 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
